issues.description: Predicate is stated by negation-of-absence rather than by the property it actually asserts.
issues.detail: The condition `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` expresses 'not a block-less layer'. The invariant is clearer phrased positively: a node is disqualifying iff it is an at-rule whose name is not in {charset, import} and is not a statement-form @layer. Rewriting in that form would make the postcondition self-evident; the current form requires the reader to simulate De Morgan in their head.

issues.description: `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is a brittle proxy for 'statement-form at-rule'.
issues.detail: The intended distinction is syntactic: does the @layer carry a block? PostCSS exposes this directly; relying on `typeof ... === 'undefined'` couples correctness to an implementation detail of the AST (e.g., `nodes` being absent vs. an empty array). State the precondition on the AST shape and check it, rather than probing for undefined.

issues.description: Test coverage exercises presence of bugs, not their absence; the dual case is unproved.
issues.detail: One positive case (`@layer foo {}` before `@import`) is added. The complementary case — statement-form `@layer foo;` before `@import`, which must remain accepted — is not asserted in this diff. Without it, the claim that the predicate distinguishes block-form from statement-form rests on inspection, not on a reasoned and tested boundary.

review.summary: The fix is small and behaviourally correct: a block-bearing @layer is no longer treated as a permitted pre-@import construct. The change is TESTED-NOT-PROVED in the strict sense — the author states no invariant for the predicate, and the predicate is written as the negation of an absence (`typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'`) rather than as the positive property it intends to assert. The diff adds one positive case but does not pin the complementary case (statement-form `@layer foo;` before `@import` must still be accepted), leaving the boundary unverified. Verdict: REASONED-ENOUGH to merge after a clearer predicate and a symmetric test; nothing here rises to refusal.
